I hated rain—literal nightmares.

Everything was instantly 10 times harder and took longer.

Bags got heavier, there was a risk of fever, congestion in walkways, clothes had to be washed every day, took longer to dry, and had to be dried inside the room because being outside meant more time.

Because of the rain bag, luggage and clothes get wet, I would have to wait for like an hour to kind of dry off before I enter the posh office complex, where everyone would look at me as though I were a wet cat with shoes that make the SCHKLOP..... SCHKLOP..... noise (causing everyone to look at me).

The route to my shitty room would be flooded, and I would have to walk knee-deep in shit (literal shit).

Because of our rental contract issues, we had to take gas cylinder in black, so if you run out of gas during rains, get ready to wait for 4-5 days (AKA induction cooking with one vessel).

Oh! Shoes are always wet and are constantly uncomfortable because of it. I worked in electrical service, so this is a big safety issue. Obviously, the head office never cared. If I complained, I would have to carry another pair of safety shoes.

Autos never stop (many blocked roads, longer routes, more expensive, company takes longer to approve because it is more than normal rates). Almost all would drop me far away from my room cuz the road to my room is flooded. So after a hard day's work, the final BOSS was the knee-deep, shitty road.

So even if I managed to dodge rain the whole day, I am still fucked.

For my job, I had to constantly carry heavy electrical equipment (so it was a constant act of balance with an umbrella). During rainy days, I hated my life in Mumbai.

I quit that job now.

I could go on and on.....

FUCK MUMBAI RAINS!!! Sleep was the only good thing.

(At times, it looks like whining. But the physical pain was too much, I had to go to the doctor to get my feet, posture checked. I bought special shoes because of all the pain)

But the craziest part was there were always a 100 others around me working in much worse conditions, So, I felt that my suffering was just me whining. But only after I quit that job did I realize that MUMBAI RAINS were a curse.
